inputs.text:
TASK: Produce a fully colored, high-quality anime manga page by editing the first input image only.

PRIORITY ORDER: 1) immutable source geometry and text, 2) complete scene colorization, 3) reference palette guidance, 4) rendering quality. If instructions conflict, follow the higher priority.

SOURCE AUTHORITY: The first input image is the sole and absolute authority for canvas, crop, panel layout, whitespace, composition, perspective, anatomy, pose, facial features, hairstyle, clothing shape, props, architecture, terrain, effects, linework, screentones, hatching, and existing light-and-shadow boundaries. Keep every existing visual boundary in the same position, size, and shape. Do not add, remove, complete, repair, simplify, or redesign visual content.

TEXT AND GRAPHICS LOCK: Speech bubbles, caption boxes, narration boxes, signs, labels, logos, and sound-effect regions are immutable source regions. Preserve their exact boundaries and white backgrounds. Copy every glyph, punctuation mark, numeral, letter, stroke, spacing, orientation, and line break exactly from the source. Keep text and black ink neutral black. Do not translate, rewrite, regenerate, restyle, move, distort, obscure, or color text.

COLOR GOAL: Apply professional anime-style cel coloring to every existing non-text region, including all visible characters, skin, hair, clothing, props, sky, vegetation, terrain, buildings, interiors, furniture, walls, floors, and objects. Use a coherent full-scene palette, natural skin tones, clear material separation, balanced saturation, and clean base colors with two or three restrained tonal levels. Treat source grayscale as the authority for structure, texture, and relative luminance, not as a requirement for the final image to remain gray. Preserve black ink, screentones, hatching, and texture beneath the color. Keep backgrounds fully colored, readable, and distinct from characters.

REFERENCE IMAGE POLICY: Additional input images are palette evidence only for matching characters, clothing, accessories, or objects already visible in the source page. Never copy a reference pose, silhouette, face, costume structure, prop shape, background, lighting layout, or composition. Ignore a reference when the match is uncertain and choose a coherent scene-local color instead. References never authorize new content.

COLOR APPLICATION: Place color beneath and within existing ink boundaries without shifting edges or tinting black outlines. Follow existing source shading when placing tonal variations. Use restrained environmental color and highlights only inside already existing regions; do not create new highlight, shadow, cloud, terrain, or object shapes. Avoid painterly rendering, photorealism, glossy effects, dramatic relighting, bloom, rim light, excessive contrast, and heavy shadows.

OUTPUT REQUIREMENT: Return the same manga page with complete color added, not a redraw or reconstruction. Geometry, line art, text, character count, object count, and scene structure must remain unchanged.
